## Lua Project

Based on the SDK's `Examples/Game Template/`:

```
MyGame/
  Source/
    main.lua        # Entry point. Must define playdate.update()
    pdxinfo         # Project metadata (required)
    images/         # Image assets (.png, compiled to .pdi by pdc)
    sounds/         # Audio assets (.wav, .mp3)
  MyGame.pdx/       # Compiled output (created by pdc)
```

## C Project

Based on the SDK's `C_API/Examples/Hello World/`:

```
MyGame/
  src/
    main.c          # Entry point. Must define eventHandler()
  Source/
    pdxinfo         # Project metadata (required)
    images/         # Assets copied into .pdx
  CMakeLists.txt    # Build config referencing playdate_game.cmake
  build/            # Build output (created by cmake)
```

## pdxinfo Format

Plain text key=value file. From the SDK docs:

```
name=b360
author=Panic Inc.
description=When all you have is a ton of bricks, everything looks like a paddle.
bundleID=com.panic.b360
version=1.0
buildNumber=123
imagePath=path/to/launcher/assets
launchSoundPath=path/to/launch/sound/file
contentWarning=This game contains mild realistic violence and bloodshed.
contentWarning2=This game contains flashing content that may not be suitable for photosensitive epilepsy.
```

Required fields: `name`, `bundleID`. Everything else is optional but recommended.

`imagePath` points to a directory containing launcher card images:
- `card.png` (350x155) -- shown in the launcher
- `icon.png` (32x32) -- shown in the system menu

`buildNumber` should be incremented for every public release.

## .pdx Bundle

The compiled game bundle. This is what the Simulator and device run.

- Created by `pdc` (Lua) or CMake + pdc (C)
- It is a directory on disk, not a single file
- Contains compiled bytecode (.pdz for Lua), compiled images (.pdi), and other assets
- Deployed to `PLAYDATE/Games/` on the device data disk

## Key SDK Paths

| Path | Description |
|---|---|
| `$PLAYDATE_SDK_PATH/bin/pdc` | Playdate compiler |
| `$PLAYDATE_SDK_PATH/bin/pdutil` | Device utility |
| `$PLAYDATE_SDK_PATH/bin/Playdate Simulator.app` | macOS simulator |
| `$PLAYDATE_SDK_PATH/CoreLibs/` | Standard Lua libraries |
| `$PLAYDATE_SDK_PATH/Examples/` | Lua example projects |
| `$PLAYDATE_SDK_PATH/C_API/pd_api.h` | C API header |
| `$PLAYDATE_SDK_PATH/C_API/Examples/` | C example projects |
| `$PLAYDATE_SDK_PATH/C_API/buildsupport/playdate_game.cmake` | CMake include for C builds |
| `$PLAYDATE_SDK_PATH/C_API/buildsupport/arm.cmake` | ARM cross-compile toolchain file |

Full docs: https://sdk.play.date/Inside%20Playdate.html

local gfx = playdate.graphics

local screenWidth = 400
local screenHeight = 240
local boardSize = 180
local cellSize = boardSize / 3
local boardX = 110
local boardY = 30
local markPadding = 14

local board = {}
local cursorX = 2
local cursorY = 2
local currentPlayer = "X"
local gameOver = false
local winner = nil

local function resetGame()
    board = {
        { nil, nil, nil },
        { nil, nil, nil },
        { nil, nil, nil },
    }
    cursorX = 2
    cursorY = 2
    currentPlayer = "X"
    gameOver = false
    winner = nil
end

local function boardFull()
    for row = 1, 3 do
        for col = 1, 3 do
            if board[row][col] == nil then
                return false
            end
        end
    end
    return true
end

local function detectWinner()
    local lines = {
        { { 1, 1 }, { 1, 2 }, { 1, 3 } },
        { { 2, 1 }, { 2, 2 }, { 2, 3 } },
        { { 3, 1 }, { 3, 2 }, { 3, 3 } },
        { { 1, 1 }, { 2, 1 }, { 3, 1 } },
        { { 1, 2 }, { 2, 2 }, { 3, 2 } },
        { { 1, 3 }, { 2, 3 }, { 3, 3 } },
        { { 1, 1 }, { 2, 2 }, { 3, 3 } },
        { { 1, 3 }, { 2, 2 }, { 3, 1 } },
    }

    for _, line in ipairs(lines) do
        local a = line[1]
        local b = line[2]
        local c = line[3]
        local first = board[a[1]][a[2]]

        if first ~= nil
            and first == board[b[1]][b[2]]
            and first == board[c[1]][c[2]] then
            return first
        end
    end

    return nil
end

local function moveCursor(dx, dy)
    cursorX = math.max(1, math.min(3, cursorX + dx))
    cursorY = math.max(1, math.min(3, cursorY + dy))
end

local function placeMark()
    if gameOver then
        return
    end

    if board[cursorY][cursorX] ~= nil then
        return
    end

    board[cursorY][cursorX] = currentPlayer
    winner = detectWinner()

    if winner ~= nil then
        gameOver = true
        return
    end

    if boardFull() then
        gameOver = true
        return
    end

    if currentPlayer == "X" then
        currentPlayer = "O"
    else
        currentPlayer = "X"
    end
end

local function drawX(x, y, size)
    gfx.drawLine(x, y, x + size, y + size)
    gfx.drawLine(x + size, y, x, y + size)
end

local function drawO(x, y, size)
    gfx.drawCircleAtPoint(x + size / 2, y + size / 2, size / 2)
end

local function drawBoard()
    for i = 1, 2 do
        local offset = i * cellSize
        gfx.drawLine(boardX + offset, boardY, boardX + offset, boardY + boardSize)
        gfx.drawLine(boardX, boardY + offset, boardX + boardSize, boardY + offset)
    end

    for row = 1, 3 do
        for col = 1, 3 do
            local mark = board[row][col]

            if mark ~= nil then
                local x = boardX + (col - 1) * cellSize + markPadding
                local y = boardY + (row - 1) * cellSize + markPadding
                local size = cellSize - markPadding * 2

                if mark == "X" then
                    drawX(x, y, size)
                else
                    drawO(x, y, size)
                end
            end
        end
    end
end

local function drawCursor()
    local x = boardX + (cursorX - 1) * cellSize
    local y = boardY + (cursorY - 1) * cellSize

    gfx.setLineWidth(3)
    gfx.drawRect(x + 2, y + 2, cellSize - 4, cellSize - 4)
    gfx.setLineWidth(1)
end

local function drawStatus()
    local status

    if winner ~= nil then
        status = winner .. " wins"
    elseif gameOver then
        status = "Draw"
    else
        status = currentPlayer .. " turn"
    end

    gfx.drawTextAligned(status, screenWidth / 2, 10, kTextAlignment.center)
    gfx.drawText("A: mark", 24, 200)
    gfx.drawText("B: reset", 24, 218)
end

resetGame()

function playdate.leftButtonDown()
    moveCursor(-1, 0)
end

function playdate.rightButtonDown()
    moveCursor(1, 0)
end

function playdate.upButtonDown()
    moveCursor(0, -1)
end

function playdate.downButtonDown()
    moveCursor(0, 1)
end

function playdate.AButtonDown()
    placeMark()
end

function playdate.BButtonDown()
    resetGame()
end

function playdate.update()
    gfx.clear(gfx.kColorWhite)
    drawStatus()
    drawBoard()
    drawCursor()
end

Analyze 4 issues with the pi-playdate extension and propose fixes based on the SDK docs and code:

**Issue 1: Build tool false negative** — "Build failed with 0 error(s)" when `isError: true`. 
Looking at `build.ts`, the `throw new Error()` path in the pdc section throws `Build failed with ${allErrors.length} error(s)`. This happens when `pdcResult.success` is false but there are 0 parsed errors. The problem is in `runPdc` — it checks exit code to determine success, but the error parsing regex may miss some error formats. Also, `pdc` may output warnings that aren't errors but still exit non-zero.

**Issue 2: Simulator PID tracking** — `open -a` on macOS spawns the .app and immediately exits. The child process we track is the `open` command, NOT the actual simulator process. So `child.pid` is the PID of `open`, which exits immediately. After that, `isSimulatorRunning()` sends signal 0 to a dead PID → returns false. This breaks screenshot + sim_log.

**Issue 3: Screenshot fails** — Because `isSimulatorRunning(state)` returns false (Issue 2), the screenshot tool refuses to run.

**Issue 4: Sim log empty** — Same root cause. Also, since `open` exits immediately, stdout/stderr pipes close immediately too. The simulator app itself writes to its own console, not to our pipes.

For Issue 2, the macOS simulator app is at `$SDK/bin/Playdate Simulator.app`. Instead of `open -a`, we could:
- Run the binary inside the .app bundle directly: `$SDK/bin/Playdate Simulator.app/Contents/MacOS/Playdate Simulator`
- Or use `pgrep` / `osascript` to find the real PID after `open`

For logs, the simulator may write to a log file. The SDK docs mention simulator features.

Propose concrete code fixes for each issue.

All checks pass. Here's a summary of what was done:

## Changes Made to `src/lib/sim.ts`

1. **Added imports**: `existsSync` from `node:fs` and `join` from `node:path`.

2. **Added `resolveSimulatorExecutable()`**: On macOS with a `.app` bundle path, builds and checks for the real binary at `<Bundle>.app/Contents/MacOS/<AppName>`. Returns it if it exists, otherwise falls back to the original path. On non-darwin, returns as-is.

3. **Replaced `open -a` block**: Removed the `let cmd/args` declarations and the macOS-specific `open -a` branch. Now uses `resolveSimulatorExecutable()` on darwin to get the actual binary, so the spawned process is the real long-lived simulator (fixing PID tracking and log capture).

4. **PID-guarded exit handler**: Captures `trackedPid` before registering `child.on("exit")`, so state is only cleared if the PID still matches — preventing stale exit events from a previous simulator instance from clobbering a newly spawned one.

Pushed. Here's what was fixed:

**Issue 1: "Build failed with 0 error(s)"** — `pdc.ts` now injects a synthetic error from the raw output when exit code is non-zero but parsing found nothing. Build error messages use output fallback instead of empty error lists.

**Issue 2: Simulator PID tracking** — Root cause was `open -a` on macOS, which spawns a short-lived launcher, not the simulator. Now launches the real binary at `Playdate Simulator.app/Contents/MacOS/Playdate Simulator` directly. Kill uses PID, exit handler is guarded against stale PIDs.

**Issue 3: Screenshot "not running"** — On macOS, the PID check is skipped entirely. `screenshotMacOS()` already validates the window via osascript.

**Issue 4: Empty sim log** — Fixed by Issue 2 (stdout/stderr now pipe from the real process). Also improved the empty message to guide users to use `print()`.

---
name: playdate
description: Develop games for the Panic Playdate handheld using the pi-playdate extension. Use when the user wants to create, build, run, or debug a Playdate game in Lua or C, work with .pdx bundles, run the Simulator, take screenshots of a running game, or deploy to a connected Playdate device over USB.
---

# Playdate Development

This skill teaches you how to develop games for the Panic Playdate using the `pi-playdate` extension. All Playdate operations go through the `playdate_*` tools -- never shell out to `pdc`, `pdutil`, `cmake`, or any SDK binary directly.

## Available Tools

| Tool | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `playdate_doctor` | Check SDK installation and environment health |
| `playdate_build` | Compile project to .pdx bundle |
| `playdate_run_sim` | Launch the Playdate Simulator |
| `playdate_stop_sim` | Stop the running simulator |
| `playdate_sim_log` | Read simulator log output |
| `playdate_screenshot` | Capture simulator screenshot |
| `playdate_run_device` | Deploy to a connected Playdate device |

## Creating a New Project

There is no scaffolding tool. Create project files directly using `write`.

Read the appropriate template reference before creating:

- **Lua project**: Read [references/templates-lua.md](references/templates-lua.md) for the required files and their contents.
- **C project**: Read [references/templates-c.md](references/templates-c.md) for the required files, CMakeLists.txt setup, and C API boilerplate.

Every project needs a `Source/pdxinfo` file. See [references/project-layout.md](references/project-layout.md) for the format.

## Typical Workflows

### New game (Lua)

1. Read `references/templates-lua.md`
2. Create `Source/main.lua` and `Source/pdxinfo` using `write`
3. `playdate_build`
4. `playdate_run_sim`
5. `playdate_screenshot` to check visuals
6. Edit code, rebuild, repeat

### New game (C)

1. Read `references/templates-c.md`
2. Create `src/main.c`, `Source/pdxinfo`, and `CMakeLists.txt` using `write`
3. `playdate_build` (auto-detects C project and uses CMake)
4. `playdate_run_sim`

Done. Two commits pushed:

**Screenshot fix:** Replaced the broken `osascript` window ID lookup (returned "missing value") with a `swift` script that queries `CGWindowListCopyWindowInfo` for the real `CGWindowID`, then passes it to `screencapture -l`. Tested and confirmed working.

**New `playdate_sim_input` tool:** Sends input to the simulator via `osascript` System Events keystrokes. Supports:
- **D-pad**: `up`, `down`, `left`, `right` (arrow keys)
- **Buttons**: `a` (keyboard 'a'), `b` (keyboard 's')
- **Menu**: clicks "Lock Screen" menu item
- **Actions**: `press` (default tap), `hold` (with configurable `duration_ms`)
- **Repeat**: send the same input multiple times

The SDK has no built-in IPC, scripting dictionary, or remote control API for the simulator. Keyboard input via System Events accessibility is the only external control mechanism available.

title: Useful Links for Playdate Development - Playdate Help
description: A list of links to video tutorials, code libraries, and other helpful resources for Playdate developers.
image: https://help.play.date/images/card-Playdate-help-library-2.png
---

# [ Useful Links for Playdate Development](/developer/dev-links/) 

Amazing people around the world are putting together video tutorials, code libraries, and other helpful resources for Playdate developers. Here’s our roundup of some we’ve seen. Please note that this information doesn’t come from Panic, and it’s not an officially supported part of the Playdate SDK.

## Learning to program Playdate

* **[The Complete Beginners Guide to Playdate Game Development](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=UZ04rk3lLqU) by SquidGod.** Complete tutorial on making games for Playdate using Lua and the Playdate SDK. Covers environment setup, code, and helpful resources.
* **[Getting Started with the Playdate SDK: Setup and Basics](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=J0ufxinp7No) by SquidGod.** 12-minute video on setting up the Playdate SDK for Windows and putting together a simple game.
* **[Everything About Playdate SDK Collisions in 7 Minutes](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=27vCPiwgWzQ) by SquidGod.** 7-minute video on collisions.
* **[Object Oriented Programming for the Playdate SDK](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=e9x6DsWk-IU) by SquidGod.** 13-minute video on object oriented programming for Playdate.
* **[Making a Roguelike for the Playdate](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=v9YBJCAa3EQ) by SquidGod.** 3-minute video starting a development log for this game project.
* **[The Beginner’s Guide to Lua for Game Development](https://squidgod.itch.io/lua-for-game-development) by SquidGod.** A book that will take you from a complete beginner to knowing the basics of coding in Lua.
* **[SquidGod’s YouTube channel](https://www.youtube.com/@SquidGodDev)** has more Playdate tutorials!
* **[Compiling Lua projects on Windows ](https://devforum.play.date/t/tutorial-compiling-lua-projects-on-windows/3332) by Tim Hei.**
* **[Playdate game development in C](https://rua.ua.es/dspace/bitstream/10045/117000/1/Playdate%5Fgame%5Fdevelopment%5Fin%5FC%5FBenavent%5FRamon%5FAlberto.pdf) by Alberto Benavent Ramón.** 87-page PDF of a Bachelor’s Thesis in Multimedia Engineering.

## Books

* **[Programming the Panic Playdate in Lua](https://www.amazon.com/Programming-Panic-Playdate-Ronald-Tanikawa/dp/B0DV96VQYQ) by Ronald Tanikawa.** Covers everything a budding Playdate Lua developer needs to know: crank APIs, sprites, music, fonts, tilemaps, and much more.
* **[Make Games for Playdate with Lua](https://leanpub.com/playdatebook) by Brett Chalupa.** Includes example games downloadable from [Github](https://github.com/brettchalupa/playdatebook).
* **[Game Design Document: A Game Development Document for the Design of 1BIT Video Games and Experiences](https://www.amazon.com/Game-Design-Document-Development-Experiences/dp/B0FP9P3MXH/ref=sr%5F1%5F1?crid=ZLGHJSRO8YY4&dib=eyJ2IjoiMSJ9.OUxxAvGvLMPHqbsoQ2wKeQ.jTLjKh5L5ieBTRjiOUbfQqVYIwJEYba-Js1uXe8NTPU&dib%5Ftag=se&keywords=playdate+console+book&qid=1757365953&sprefix=playdate+console+boo%2Caps%2C129&sr=8-1) by Brian Jameson.** A beautiful, blank notebook for all of your Playdate game ideas. Includes templates for sprites, tiles, game mechanics… you name it.

## Libraries

* **[Timeline for Playdate](https://github.com/mierau/playdate-timeline) by Dustin Mierau.**A Lua library designed to make it easier to compose animations and events in your game code over time. See some of Dustin’s remarkable animations at work in [_Playmaker_](https://play.date/games/playmaker/).
* **[Noble Engine](https://github.com/NobleRobot/NobleEngine) by Mark LaCroix.**A li’l game engine for Playdate.
* **[AnimatedSprite](https://github.com/Whitebrim/AnimatedSprite) by Whitebrim.** Sprite class extension that covers animations, finite state machine, and JSON loading.
* **[Taxman Engine](https://github.com/McDevon/taxman-engine) by Jussi Enroos.** 2D Game Engine for Playdate and other platforms.
* **[Panels](https://github.com/cadin/panels) by Cadin Batrack.** Build interactive comics for the Playdate console.
* **[A list of helpful libraries and code](https://devforum.play.date/t/a-list-of-helpful-libraries-and-code/221) by Dev Forum members.** A thread of helpful libraries and small bits of code, started and maintained by our Dev Forum members.

## Coding Tools

* **[Nova](https://nova.app) by Panic.** You can use any code editor you like with our SDK. We happen to make a pretty nice one for macOS, and it’s great for Playdate development, with easy building and debugging.
* **[pdmanager](https://apps.apple.com/us/app/pdmanager/id6751735648) by Keith Baker.** Mac app that connects to and lets you manage your Playdate—organize games, back up saves, track achivements, and more.
* **[Playdate Debug for VS Code](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug) by midouest.** Unofficial Playdate debug extension for Visual Studio Code on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu.
* **[VS Code Playdate Template (Windows & Linux)](https://github.com/Whitebrim/VSCode-PlaydateTemplate) by Whitebrim.** A template for autocompletion and running your code in the Playdate Simulator on Windows and Linux.
* **[Playdate VS Code Template (Mac)](https://github.com/cadin/playdate-vscode-template) by Cadin Batrack.** VS Code template with tasks for building and running in Playdate simulator on macOS.
* **[Playdate Types](https://github.com/balpha/playdate-types) by Benjamin Dumke-von der Ehe.** Type annotations for the Playdate Lua SDK.
* **[LuaCATS](https://github.com/notpeter/playdate-luacats) by Peter Tripp.** LuaCATS is a way to provide machine-readable Lua type annotations and comments, enabling inline autocompletion and linting suggestions.

## Graphics & Fonts

* **[Caps](https://play.date/caps) by Panic.** Panic’s official bitmap-font editor for Playdate fonts. Draw your own typographic characters, edit existing fonts, kern and preview them—all right here.
* **[Playdate Arcade Fonts](https://github.com/idleberg/playdate-arcade-fonts) by Jan T. Sott.** A growing collection of bitmap fonts based on classic arcade games.
* **[Playdate Art: Scale](https://donaldhays.com/2019/12/30/playdate-art-scale/) by Donald Hays.** Thoughts and observations on Playdate art, with a focus on choosing the size to make your art tiles and sprites.
* **[Tophat](https://kaasiand.cool/tophat/) by Kaasiand.** A powerful tool to create bitmap fonts for use with the Playdate SDK.
* **[PDFontTool](https://github.com/abenokobo/PDFontTool) by Takuya.** Command line tool for Windows that converts Windows-supported fonts such as TrueType Font, OpenType Font, etc. into fonts for Playdate.

## Languages

* **[Byte-sized Swift: Building Tiny Games for the Playdate](https://www.swift.org/blog/byte-sized-swift-tiny-games-playdate/) by the Swift Team.** The Swift team’s new embedded language support means you can target platforms like Playdate via Swift.
* **[PlaydateKit](https://github.com/finnvoor/PlaydateKit) by Finn Voorhees.** Swift bindings for the Playdate C SDK.
* **[Crankscript](https://github.com/crankscript/crankscript)**. A rich framework allowing devs to author Playdate games in TypeScript.
* **[Playdate-C++](https://github.com/nstbayless/playdate-cpp) by Metaphaseaudio.** C++ on Playdate.
* **[Playdate C++ Extensions](https://github.com/metaphaseaudio/playdate-cpp-extensions) by Metaphaseaudio.** Classes and functions to assist with development for the Playdate in C++.
* **[Rust for Playdate](https://github.com/pd-rs/crankstart) by Rob Tsuk and Alexander Koz.** “A barely functional, wildly incomplete and basically undocumented Rust crate whose aim is to let you write Games for the Playdate handheld gaming system in Rust.”
* **[Go for Playdate](https://github.com/playdate-go/pdgo) by Roman Bielyi.** _pdgo_ is an open-source project providing Go compiler support, SDK bindings, tools, and examples for developing games and applications on Playdate.
* **[Nim Playdate](https://github.com/samdze/playdate-nim) by Samuele Zolfanelli.** Nim bindings with extra features for the Playdate SDK.
* **[Zig Template for Playdate](https://github.com/DanB91/Zig-Playdate-Template) by DanB91.** Use this template as a starting point to write your Playdate games in Zig.

## Devlogs

* **[_Atlantic ‘41_](https://stephanrewind.itch.io/atlantic-41) by Stephan Rewind.** A tremendously detailed World War 2 U-boat simulation.
* **[_Diora_](https://dioragame.com/devlog/) by Zachary Snyder.** Devlog of an isometric 3D game.
* **[_Mars After Midnight_ development log](https://dukope.itch.io/mars-after-midnight) by Lucas Pope.** _Papers, Please_ and _Return of the Obra Dinn_’s creator’s posts about the development of his Playdate game.
* **[_Pullfrog_ development log](https://amano.games/devlog) by Amano Games.** Tetris meets frog.

## Playdate Resources Elsewhere

* **[Playdate Stuff](https://github.com/stars/filmgirl/lists/playdate-stuff) by Christina Warren.** Cool Things for Panic’s Playdate.
* **[Awesome Playdate](https://github.com/sayhiben/awesome-playdate) by Ben Menesini.** A list of awesome resources for Playdate game development and the Playdate SDK.
* **[SDK Resources](https://playdate-wiki.com/wiki/Developing%5Ffor%5FPlaydate) by Playdate Community Wiki.** A list of resources that are available for free to help you with developing games on Playdate.

## Pulp

We also have a list of resources you may find helpful when making games in [Pulp](/developer/pulp-links).

[If you didn't find an answer above, contact us](/contact/)

content.text:
Here’s what the source code shows (without relying on README): this extension’s **debug adapter implementation is a TCP proxy layer, not a custom Playdate protocol implementation**.

## 1) How it connects to the simulator (TCP? what port?)

It uses **TCP sockets**:

- `ProxyDebugAdapterDescriptorFactory` creates a `ProxyServer`, then exposes it to VS Code as a `DebugAdapterServer` on an ephemeral local port (`listen(0)`, then `server.address().port`). [ProxyDebugAdapterDescriptorFactory.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/ProxyDebugAdapterDescriptorFactory.ts)
- `ProxyServer.start(...)` creates a local net server and also connects out to the simulator using `waitForDebugPort(SIMULATOR_DEBUG_PORT, ...)`. [ProxyServer.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/ProxyServer.ts)
- The simulator port is hard-coded as `55934` in `SIMULATOR_DEBUG_PORT` with comment saying it is the Playdate Simulator DAP port. [constants.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/constants.ts)

Connection retry behavior:
- `waitForDebugPort` does repeated `net.createConnection({ port })` attempts with configurable retry timeout / max retries (defaults are in code). [waitForDebugPort.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/util/waitForDebugPort.ts)

So the flow is:

```
VS Code debug client <--> local ProxyServer (local ephemeral port) <--> Playdate Simulator at tcp:55934
```

---

## 2) What messages/commands are sent (evaluate Lua? button input?)

No custom Playdate-specific command dispatcher is implemented here.  
The adapter is a **generic proxy** for DAP traffic:

- If workaround mode is enabled, it decodes each incoming DAP frame, optionally applies fixes, and forwards the message to simulator. [ProxyServer.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/ProxyServer.ts)
- If workaround mode is disabled, it forwards buffers unchanged in both directions. [ProxyServer.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/ProxyServer.ts)

Workarounds only touch a small set of protocol messages:
- synthetic/modified responses for `launch`, `restart`  
- tweak `initialize` capabilities (`supportsRestartRequest`, `supportsTerminateRequest`)  
- enforce `variablesReference = 0` when missing in `variables`  
- mark breakpoints verified in `setBreakpoints` response  
[FixLaunchResponse.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/fix/FixLaunchResponse.ts), [FixRestartResponse.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/fix/FixRestartResponse.ts), [FixSupportsRestartRequest.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/fix/FixSupportsRestartRequest.ts), [FixSupportsTerminateRequest.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/fix/FixSupportsTerminateRequest.ts), [FixVariablesReference.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/fix/FixVariablesReference.ts), [FixBreakpointVerified.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/fix/FixBreakpointVerified.ts)

So: **no explicit handling here for custom “button input” commands** in the adapter; that kind of input is not implemented in the debug adapter codebase.

---

## 3) How it sends Lua commands to running simulator

There is no dedicated “Lua command sender” method in this adapter.  
It proxies DAP messages as-is. So if your client/session sends an `evaluate` request (or any other DAP request like stepping, variables, breakpoints), it is passed through to the simulator’s DAP server. [ProxyServer.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/ProxyServer.ts)

The only time it generates/sends something itself is via workaround fixes (e.g. synthetic `launch`/`restart` response objects). [FixLaunchResponse.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/fix/FixLaunchResponse.ts), [FixRestartResponse.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/fix/FixRestartResponse.ts)

---

## 4) Screenshot/display capture capability?

No screenshot/display capture functionality is present in the debug adapter implementation.  
The `src/debug` module only contains:
- proxy server/factory/logger and
- protocol fix classes  
(as shown by directory contents), [src/debug listing](https://api.github.com/repos/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/contents/src/debug?ref=main).  
No command/event handling for screenshot/capture appears in these adapter files.

So **not in this adapter layer**.

---

## 5) Message format: JSON or raw text?

It uses **DAP-over-socket with `Content-Length` framing and JSON payloads** (standard Debug Adapter Protocol base framing):

- Decoder expects each message as `Content-Length: <n>\r\n\r\n<JSON>` and parses JSON. [ProxyServer.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/ProxyServer.ts)
- Encoder does `Buffer.from("Content-Length: " + content.length + "\r\n\r\n" + JSON.stringify(message))`. [ProxyServer.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/ProxyServer.ts)

This is classic DAP raw text framing over TCP, not protobuf/binary or custom JSON-RPC variant.

---

### Extra notable detail
- Debug adapter behavior has toggles in `launch.json`/`attach` config:
  - `logDebugAdapter`
  - `disableWorkarounds`
  - `retryTimeout`, `maxRetries`  
  [package.json debug configuration](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/package.json)

If you want, I can map the exact path of a sample DAP `evaluate` message as it would pass through this proxy (input JSON → encode/decode → forward).

# Playdate Debug

[![tests](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/actions/workflows/tests.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/actions/workflows/tests.yaml)

Unofficial Playdate debug extension for Visual Studio Code on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu

## Features

- Debug Lua code running in the Playdate Simulator
- Compile games to `.pdx` using `pdc`
- Problem matchers for `pdc`
- Open the Playdate Simulator
- Run and debug current Lua file in the Playdate Simulator from the editor toolbar

## Requirements

- The [Playdate SDK](https://play.date/dev/) must be installed separately

## Quick setup

### Tasks and debug launcher

Copy the following `.vscode/tasks.json` and `.vscode/launch.json` configuration:

```json
// .vscode/tasks.json
{
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "tasks": [
    {
      "type": "pdc",
      "problemMatcher": ["$pdc-lua", "$pdc-external"],
      "label": "Playdate: Build"
    },
    {
      "type": "playdate-simulator",
      "problemMatcher": ["$pdc-external"],
      "label": "Playdate: Run"
    },
    {
      "label": "Playdate: Build and Run",
      "dependsOn": ["Playdate: Build", "Playdate: Run"],
      "dependsOrder": "sequence",
      "problemMatcher": [],
      "group": {
        "kind": "build",
        "isDefault": true
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
// .vscode/launch.json
{
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "configurations": [
    {
      "type": "playdate",
      "request": "launch",
      "name": "Playdate: Debug",
      "preLaunchTask": "${defaultBuildTask}"
    }
  ]
}
```

The debugger can be launched from the "Run and Debug view" by selecting the "Playdate: Debug" launch configuration and then clicking the "Start Debugging" button.

![Run and Debug view](/images/run-and-debug-view.png)

![Start Debugging](/images/start-debugging.png)

A [cookiecutter project template](https://github.com/midouest/cookiecutter-playdate) is available for quickly generating new projects with the above configuration from the command line.

See the [basic configuration example](/fixtures/workspace/basic-configuration) for more information.

### Run and debug current Lua file

**NOTE:** The "Run/Debug file in Playdate Simulator" command is intended to be a shortcut for prototyping and learning. It is recommended to use the [task and launch configuration above](#tasks-and-debug-launcher).

The extension can build, run and debug the current Lua file in the editor with zero configuration as long the [automatic configuration conditions](#automatic) are met.

When you open a Lua file in the editor after installing the extension, you will now see a
launch icon and dropdown menu in the editor toolbar. Clicking the launch icon or selecting an item from the dropdown menu will build and run the current Lua file in the Playdate Simulator. The "Debug file in Playdate Simulator" option will enable breakpoints to be hit.

![Tooltip](/images/tooltip.png)

![Dropdown Menu](/images/dropdown-menu.png)

## Configuration

### Automatic

The tasks and debugger will attempt to automatically resolve the correct configuration using the environment. One of the following conditions must be met for this to work:

- The `PLAYDATE_SDK_PATH` environment variable is set to the Playdate SDK path
- `~/.Playdate/config` exists and the `SDKRoot` property is set to the Playdate SDK path (macOS only)

### Workspace settings override

The default behavior can be overridden by setting the SDK path, game source path, compiled game path or game name in your workspace's `settings.json` file. The extension will fall back to the default behavior for any configuration fields that are not set.

```json
// .vscode/settings.json
{
  "playdate-debug.sdkPath": "/path/to/PlaydateSDK",
  "playdate-debug.sourcePath": "/path/to/MyGame/source",
  "playdate-debug.outputPath": "/path/to/MyGame",
  "playdate-debug.productName": "My Game"
}
```

See the [override configuration example](/fixtures/workspace/override-configuration) for more information about these properties.

### PDC task

See the [pdc configuration example](/fixtures/workspace/pdc-configuration/) for additional `pdc` task properties.

### Playdate Simulator task

See the [playdate simulator configuration example](/fixtures/workspace/playdate-simulator-configuration/) for additional `playdate-simulator` task properties.

### Debugger

See the [debugger configuration example](/fixtures/workspace/debugger-configuration/) for additional `playdate` debugger properties.

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [1.20.2]

### Fixed

- Killing the simulator on macOS

## [1.20.0] - 2025-10-08

### Added

- Playdate Simulator task `argv` option can send additional args to the Playdate game

## [1.18.0] - 2025-01-11

### Added

- `libPath` PDC option

## [1.16.0] - 2023-10-22

### Added

- Debugger can attach to running games instead of launching them

### Fixed

- pdc error when building a project that uses relative imports

## [1.14.10] - 2023-08-06

### Fixed

- Prevent accidentally including PlaydateSDK test fixtures in the release bundle

## [1.14.8] - 2023-08-05

### Fixed

- Increment and save build number before compiling instead of after

## [1.14.6] - 2023-04-23

### Fixed

- "Run/debug file in Playdate Simulator" command is compatible with Playdate SDK 1.13.5

## [1.14.4] - 2023-04-12

### Fixed

- Extension can display very large stack traces

## [1.14.1] - 2023-03-25

### Changed

- Show error message on windows and linux when Playdate SDK version does not support debugging

### Fixed

- The Linux simulator task correctly handles game paths with spaces

## [1.14.0] - 2023-02-14

### Changed

- Extension no longer launches simulator in gnome-terminal on Linux

## [1.12.0] - 2023-02-10

### Changed

- Extended default timeout to 10 seconds

### Fixed

- Extension waits for simulator to launch before connecting to debug adapter in SDK 1.13

## [1.10.0] - 2023-01-08

### Changed

- Run/debug editor contents command stops running playdate debug sessions

### Fixed

- `incrementBuildNumber` only outputs keys that are present in the original file

## [1.9.1] - 2022-12-10

### Fixed

- Clean up correctly after run/debug current file

## [1.9.0] - 2022-12-10

### Added

- `incrementBuildNumber` configuration option on `pdc` task will auto-increment the pdxinfo buildNumber property after each successful build
- `outputPath` workspace configuration option can be used to output to `/Disk/Games` folder in the Playdate SDK

## [1.8.2] - 2022-11-21

### Added

- Run and debug current Lua file as main.lua

### Changed

- Display error messages from commands and tasks
- Completely disable proxy server when disableWorkarounds is enabled

### Fixed

- Problem matchers correctly match absolute file paths
- Example project links in readme link to project folders

## [1.7.0] - 2022-11-19

### Added

- Support for multi-root workspaces

### Changed

- Completely disable proxy server for SDK version 1.13.0 or later
- Streamlined quick setup in README

### Fixed

- Check PLAYDATE_SDK_PATH environment variable before checking ~.Playdate/config

## [1.6.0] - 2022-11-18

### Added

- Relative paths in settings.json are now resolved from the workspace root
- Breakpoints are in a verified state

### Changed

- Only check for ~/.Playdate on macOS
- Automatically disable workarounds in SDK version 1.13.0 and later
- Extension now waits up to 5 seconds to connect by default

### Fixed

- PDC task sends correct CLI flag for skipUnknown setting
- PDC task always sends -sdkpath

## [1.5.1] - 2022-11-14

### Changed

- Log task commands before they are executed

### Fixed

- Increased maximum number of retries and retry timeout when attempting to connect to the Playdate Simulator. The extension now waits up to 4 seconds to connect by default.
- Log proxied messages before attempting to decode them
- Fixed an issue where the extension incorrectly decoded debug adapter messages sent from Visual Studio Code v1.73+

## [1.5.0] - 2022-10-13

### Added

- Retry timeout and maximum number of retries are configurable in launch.json

### Fixed

- Increased maximum number of retries when attempting to connect to the Playdate Simulator

## [1.4.1] - 2022-09-28

### Fixed

- Fix incorrect settings in docs

## [1.4.0] - 2022-09-06

### Added

- Ensure VSCode UI resets when restarting after an exception occurs
- `pdc` task supports strip, no-compress, verbose, quiet and skip-unknown flags

### Removed

- `timeout` property on `pdc` task

### Fixed

- `pdc` task compiles to fully-resolved `.pdx` path instead of output folder
- Account for `pdc` binary path with spaces - [@NobleRobot](https://github.com/NobleRobot)

## [1.3.2] - 2022-08-01

### Changed

- README contains link to template project

## [1.3.1] - 2022-07-05

### Changed

- `pdc` task no longer requires `pdc` command to be in the `PATH` variable

## [1.3.0] - 2022-07-02

### Added

- `disableWorkarounds` property on launch configuration to disable workarounds for issues communicating between VSCode and the Playdate Simulator.

## [1.2.0] - 2022-07-02

### Added

- `logDebugAdapter` property on launch configuration to log communication between VSCode and the Playdate Simulator

## [1.1.3] - 2022-07-01

### Fixed

Unofficial Playdate debug extension for Visual Studio Code on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu Features Debug Lua code running in the Playdate Simulator Compile games to .pdx using pdc Problem matchers for pdc Open the Playdate Simulator Run and debug current Lua file in the Playdate Simulator from the editor toolbar Requirements The [Playdate SDK](https://play.date/dev/) must be installed separately Quick setup Tasks and debug launcher Copy the following .vscode/tasks.json and .vscode/launch.json configuration: // .vscode/tasks.json {   "version": "2.0.0",   "tasks": \[     {       "type": "pdc",       "problemMatcher": \["$pdc-lua", "$pdc-external"\],       "label": "Playdate: Build"     },     {       "type": "playdate-simulator",       "problemMatcher": \["$pdc-external"\],       "label": "Playdate: Run"     },     {       "label": "Playdate: Build and Run",       "dependsOn": \["Playdate: Build", "Playdate: Run"\],       "dependsOrder": "sequence",       "problemMatcher": \[\],       "group": {         "kind": "build",         "isDefault": true       }     }   \] } // .vscode/launch.json {   "version": "0.2.0",   "configurations": \[     {       "type": "playdate",       "request": "launch",       "name": "Playdate: Debug",       "preLaunchTask": "${defaultBuildTask}"     }   \] } The debugger can be launched from the "Run and Debug view" by selecting the "Playdate: Debug" launch configuration and then clicking the "Start Debugging" button. ![Run and Debug view](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/raw/HEAD/images/run-and-debug-view.png) ![Start Debugging](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/raw/HEAD/images/start-debugging.png) A [cookiecutter project template](https://github.com/midouest/cookiecutter-playdate) is available for quickly generating new projects with the above configuration from the command line. See the [basic configuration example](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/HEAD/fixtures/workspace/basic-configuration) for more information. Run and debug current Lua file **NOTE:** The "Run/Debug file in Playdate Simulator" command is intended to be a shortcut for prototyping and learning. It is recommended to use the [task and launch configuration above](#tasks-and-debug-launcher). The extension can build, run and debug the current Lua file in the editor with zero configuration as long the [automatic configuration conditions](#automatic) are met. When you open a Lua file in the editor after installing the extension, you will now see a launch icon and dropdown menu in the editor toolbar. Clicking the launch icon or selecting an item from the dropdown menu will build and run the current Lua file in the Playdate Simulator. The "Debug file in Playdate Simulator" option will enable breakpoints to be hit. ![Tooltip](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/raw/HEAD/images/tooltip.png) ![Dropdown Menu](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/raw/HEAD/images/dropdown-menu.png) Configuration Automatic The tasks and debugger will attempt to automatically resolve the correct configuration using the environment. One of the following conditions must be met for this to work: The PLAYDATE\_SDK\_PATH environment variable is set to the Playdate SDK path \~/.Playdate/config exists and the SDKRoot property is set to the Playdate SDK path (macOS only) Workspace settings override The default behavior can be overridden by setting the SDK path, game source path, compiled game path or game name in your workspace's settings.json file. The extension will fall back to the default behavior for any configuration fields that are not set. // .vscode/settings.json {   "playdate-debug.sdkPath": "/path/to/PlaydateSDK",   "playdate-debug.sourcePath": "/path/to/MyGame/source",   "playdate-debug.outputPath": "/path/to/MyGame",   "playdate-debug.productName": "My Game" } See the [override configuration example](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/HEAD/fixtures/workspace/override-configuration) for more information about these properties. Issue body actions

Hi,

Would it be possible to debug projects written in C? I'm using the Sprite Game example from the SDK's C\_API directory to test with it, and while I can get a debug build running in the simulator, attempting to launch the game with this extension causes it to exit silently (neither the simulator console nor the client/server debug log generated by the extension give any indication as to why).

My understanding is that this extension only supports Lua projects, so I'm not surprised it doesn't work for C, but I'd like to know what it would take to add support for that. Happy to contribute with a PR if you can give me some pointers!

Thanks

 "body": "## Problem Description\n\nThe `vscode-playdate-debug` extension's task providers (`pdc` and `playdate-simulator`) fail to create tasks even with correct configuration. The error message is:\n\n```\nError: The pdc task detection didn't contribute a task for the following configuration:\n{\n \"label\": \"Playdate: Build\",\n \"type\": \"pdc\",\n \"problemMatcher\": [\"$pdc-lua\", \"$pdc-external\"],\n \"presentation\": { ... }\n}\nThe task will be ignored.\n```\n\n## Environment\n\n- **VS Code Version**: 2.0.64 (arm64)\n- **Playdate SDK Version**: 3.0.1\n- **Extension Version**: midouest.playdate-debug (latest from marketplace)\n- **OS**: macOS (darwin 25.1.0)\n- **SDK Path**: `/Users/mateuszbronis/Developer/PlaydateSDK` (auto-detected from `~/.Playdate/config`)\n\n## Configuration\n\n### `.vscode/tasks.json` (minimal example from documentation)\n\n```json\n{\n \"version\": \"2.0.0\",\n \"tasks\": [\n {\n \"label\": \"Playdate: Build\",\n \"type\": \"pdc\",\n \"problemMatcher\": [\"$pdc-lua\", \"$pdc-external\"]\n },\n {\n \"label\": \"Playdate: Run\",\n \"type\": \"playdate-simulator\",\n \"problemMatcher\": [\"$pdc-external\"]\n }\n ]\n}\n```\n\n### `.vscode/settings.json`\n\n```json\n{\n \"playdate-debug.sourcePath\": \"source\",\n \"playdate-debug.outputPath\": \"builds\",\n \"playdate-debug.productName\": \"Game\"\n}\n```\n\n### `~/.Playdate/config`\n\n```\nSDKRoot /Users/mateuszbronis/Developer/PlaydateSDK\n```\n\n## Steps to Reproduce\n\n1. Install `vscode-playdate-debug` extension\n2. Create a Playdate project with `source/` directory containing `main.lua` and `pdxinfo`\n3. Configure `tasks.json` with task types `pdc` and `playdate-simulator` (as shown in documentation)\n4. Configure `settings.json` with `playdate-debug.sourcePath`, `playdate-debug.outputPath`, and `playdate-debug.productName`\n5. Ensure `task.autoDetect` is enabled in VS Code settings (default should be `\"on\"`)\n6. Reload VS Code window\n7. Observe error in Output panel: \"task detection didn't contribute a task\"\n\n**Note**: `task.autoDetect` is confirmed to be set to `\"on\"` in workspace settings, so this is not the cause of the issue.\n\n## Expected Behavior\n\nThe extension should automatically create tasks based on the configuration in `settings.json` and `~/.Playdate/config`, allowing the tasks to be executed.\n\n## Actual Behavior\n\nTasks are not created, and the error \"task detection didn't contribute a task\" appears in the Output panel.\n\n## Workaround\n\nUsing shell tasks works correctly:\n\n```json\n{\n \"label\": \"Playdate: Build\",\n \"type\": \"shell\",\n \"command\": \"pdc\",\n \"args\": [\n \"${workspaceFolder}/source\",\n \"${workspaceFolder}/builds/Game.pdx\"\n ]\n}\n```\n\n## Possible Root Cause\n\nBased on troubleshooting guides and similar issues with other VS Code extensions, the problem may be related to:\n\n1. **Task provider implementation bug**: The task provider appears to be failing to create tasks despite correct configuration. This suggests a bug in the task provider's `resolveTask` or `provideTasks` implementation. The task provider may be failing to:\n - Read workspace settings (`playdate-debug.*`)\n - Resolve relative paths from workspace root\n - Validate that required directories exist before creating tasks\n - Handle the case where `productName` is required but not automatically detected from `pdxinfo`\n\n## Suggested Fix\n\n### For Users (Workaround)\n\nUse shell tasks as a workaround (see Workaround section). The `task.autoDetect` setting is confirmed to be enabled, so the issue is in the extension's task provider implementation.\n\n### For Extension Developers\n\nThe task provider should:\n\n1. **Check `task.autoDetect` setting**: The extension should warn users if `task.autoDetect` is disabled, as this prevents task providers from working\n2. Validate that `sourcePath` and `outputPath` exist or can be resolved\n3. Automatically detect `productName` from `pdxinfo` if not explicitly set\n4. details.response:
Here’s what the source code shows (without relying on README): this extension’s **debug adapter implementation is a TCP proxy layer, not a custom Playdate protocol implementation**.

## 1) How it connects to the simulator (TCP? what port?)

It uses **TCP sockets**:

- `ProxyDebugAdapterDescriptorFactory` creates a `ProxyServer`, then exposes it to VS Code as a `DebugAdapterServer` on an ephemeral local port (`listen(0)`, then `server.address().port`). [ProxyDebugAdapterDescriptorFactory.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/ProxyDebugAdapterDescriptorFactory.ts)
- `ProxyServer.start(...)` creates a local net server and also connects out to the simulator using `waitForDebugPort(SIMULATOR_DEBUG_PORT, ...)`. [ProxyServer.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/ProxyServer.ts)
- The simulator port is hard-coded as `55934` in `SIMULATOR_DEBUG_PORT` with comment saying it is the Playdate Simulator DAP port. [constants.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/constants.ts)

Connection retry behavior:
- `waitForDebugPort` does repeated `net.createConnection({ port })` attempts with configurable retry timeout / max retries (defaults are in code). [waitForDebugPort.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/util/waitForDebugPort.ts)

So the flow is:

```
VS Code debug client <--> local ProxyServer (local ephemeral port) <--> Playdate Simulator at tcp:55934
```

---

## 2) What messages/commands are sent (evaluate Lua? button input?)

No custom Playdate-specific command dispatcher is implemented here.  
The adapter is a **generic proxy** for DAP traffic:

- If workaround mode is enabled, it decodes each incoming DAP frame, optionally applies fixes, and forwards the message to simulator. [ProxyServer.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/ProxyServer.ts)
- If workaround mode is disabled, it forwards buffers unchanged in both directions. [ProxyServer.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/ProxyServer.ts)

Workarounds only touch a small set of protocol messages:
- synthetic/modified responses for `launch`, `restart`  
- tweak `initialize` capabilities (`supportsRestartRequest`, `supportsTerminateRequest`)  
- enforce `variablesReference = 0` when missing in `variables`  
- mark breakpoints verified in `setBreakpoints` response  
[FixLaunchResponse.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/fix/FixLaunchResponse.ts), [FixRestartResponse.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/fix/FixRestartResponse.ts), [FixSupportsRestartRequest.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/fix/FixSupportsRestartRequest.ts), [FixSupportsTerminateRequest.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/fix/FixSupportsTerminateRequest.ts), [FixVariablesReference.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/fix/FixVariablesReference.ts), [FixBreakpointVerified.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/fix/FixBreakpointVerified.ts)

So: **no explicit handling here for custom “button input” commands** in the adapter; that kind of input is not implemented in the debug adapter codebase.

---

## 3) How it sends Lua commands to running simulator

There is no dedicated “Lua command sender” method in this adapter.  
It proxies DAP messages as-is. So if your client/session sends an `evaluate` request (or any other DAP request like stepping, variables, breakpoints), it is passed through to the simulator’s DAP server. [ProxyServer.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/ProxyServer.ts)

The only time it generates/sends something itself is via workaround fixes (e.g. synthetic `launch`/`restart` response objects). [FixLaunchResponse.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/fix/FixLaunchResponse.ts), [FixRestartResponse.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/fix/FixRestartResponse.ts)

---

## 4) Screenshot/display capture capability?

No screenshot/display capture functionality is present in the debug adapter implementation.  
The `src/debug` module only contains:
- proxy server/factory/logger and
- protocol fix classes  
(as shown by directory contents), [src/debug listing](https://api.github.com/repos/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/contents/src/debug?ref=main).  
No command/event handling for screenshot/capture appears in these adapter files.

So **not in this adapter layer**.

---

## 5) Message format: JSON or raw text?

It uses **DAP-over-socket with `Content-Length` framing and JSON payloads** (standard Debug Adapter Protocol base framing):

- Decoder expects each message as `Content-Length: <n>\r\n\r\n<JSON>` and parses JSON. [ProxyServer.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/ProxyServer.ts)
- Encoder does `Buffer.from("Content-Length: " + content.length + "\r\n\r\n" + JSON.stringify(message))`. [ProxyServer.ts](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/debug/ProxyServer.ts)

This is classic DAP raw text framing over TCP, not protobuf/binary or custom JSON-RPC variant.

---

### Extra notable detail
- Debug adapter behavior has toggles in `launch.json`/`attach` config:
  - `logDebugAdapter`
  - `disableWorkarounds`
  - `retryTimeout`, `maxRetries`  
  [package.json debug configuration](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/package.json)

If you want, I can map the exact path of a sample DAP `evaluate` message as it would pass through this proxy (input JSON → encode/decode → forward).

Excellent. The simulator has a **DAP (Debug Adapter Protocol) server on TCP port 55934**. This means we can:

1. **Evaluate Lua code** via DAP `evaluate` requests -- including `playdate.simulator.writeToFile()` for screenshots and `playdate.buttonIsPressed()` for reading state
2. **Read variables, set breakpoints, step through code** -- standard debugger operations
3. **Send `evaluate` to run arbitrary Lua** in the simulator context

arguments.command:
# Test DAP connection to the simulator on port 55934
# DAP format: Content-Length: <n>\r\n\r\n<JSON>

# Send an initialize request
python3 -c "
import socket, json, time

def send_dap(sock, msg):
    body = json.dumps(msg)
    header = f'Content-Length: {len(body)}\r\n\r\n'
    sock.sendall((header + body).encode())

def recv_dap(sock, timeout=3):
    sock.settimeout(timeout)
    data = b''
    try:
        while True:
            chunk = sock.recv(4096)
            if not chunk:
                break
            data += chunk
    except socket.timeout:
        pass
    return data.decode('utf-8', errors='replace')

s = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM)
s.connect(('127.0.0.1', 55934))

# Initialize
send_dap(s, {
    'seq': 1,
    'type': 'request',
    'command': 'initialize',
    'arguments': {
        'clientID': 'pi-playdate',
        'clientName': 'Pi Playdate',
        'adapterID': 'playdate',
        'pathFormat': 'path',
        'linesStartAt1': True,
        'columnsStartAt1': True,
    }
})

time.sleep(0.5)
response = recv_dap(s, 1)
print('=== Initialize Response ===')
print(response[:2000])

# Try evaluate
send_dap(s, {
    'seq': 2,
    'type': 'request',
    'command': 'evaluate',
    'arguments': {
        'expression': 'print(\"hello from DAP\")',
        'context': 'repl',
    }
})

time.sleep(0.5)
response2 = recv_dap(s, 1)
print('=== Evaluate Response ===')
print(response2[:2000])

s.close()
" 2>&1

def send_dap(sock, msg):

def recv_dap_messages(sock, timeout=3):
    sock.settimeout(timeout)
    data = b''
    try:
        while True:
            chunk = sock.recv(4096)
            if not chunk:
                break
            data += chunk
    except socket.timeout:
        pass
    
    messages = []
    while data:
        # Find Content-Length header
        idx = data.find(b'\r\n\r\n')
        if idx == -1:
            break
        header = data[:idx].decode('utf-8')
        content_length = None
        for line in header.split('\r\n'):

        body_start = idx + 4

# [Playdate Simulator debug adapter protocol does not support terminate request](/t/playdate-simulator-debug-adapter-protocol-does-not-support-terminate-request/4162) 

[ SDK Bug Reports ](/c/sdk-bugs/47) 

[midouest](https://devforum.play.date/u/midouest)  March 22, 2022, 1:09am 1 

**Platform**  
macOS

**Reproduction**  
This bug does not affect debugging in Nova, but it does have a minor affect on debugging in VS Code.

I am inspecting the messages between the client and the Playdate Simulator debugger using `sudo tcpdump -i lo0 -A tcp port 55934` .

1. Open a Playdate project
2. Build the project
3. Debug the game using the Playdate Simulator debugger
4. Press the stop button in the client

**Expected**

1. The client sends: `{ "command":"initialize", "type":"request" }`
2. The server responds with: `{ "command":"initialize", "type":"response", "success":true,", "supportsTerminateRequest":true }`
3. The client sends: `{ "type": "request", "command": "terminate" }`
4. The server responds with: `{ "type": "response", "command": "terminate", "success": true }`

**Actual**

1. The client sends: `{ "command":"initialize", "type":"request" }`
2. The server responds with: `{ "command":"initialize", "type":"response", "success":true,", "supportsTerminateRequest":true }`
3. The client sends: `{ "type": "request", "command": "terminate" }`
4. The server responds with: `{"command":"terminate","message":"Unsupported method: terminate","type":"response","success":false}`

I see that Nova sends a `disconnect` command instead of a `terminate` command. VS Code attempts to send a `terminate` command first and then a `disconnect` command second if the `terminate` fails as mentioned in this [issue](https://github.com/microsoft/debug-adapter-protocol/issues/249#issuecomment-1073811908).

[midouest](https://devforum.play.date/u/midouest)  March 23, 2022, 2:24am 2 

I was able to work around this issue and [Playdate Simulator debug adapter protocol does not send success response to launch request](https://devforum.play.date/t/playdate-simulator-debug-adapter-protocol-does-not-send-success-response-to-launch-request/4161) by proxying messages to and from the Simulator: <https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/src/PlaydateDebugAdapterProxy.ts>

Patching the `supportsTerminateRequest` property now causes VS Code to correctly terminate the debugger when the user clicks the stop button.

Here is a working example of how it is written in the same room(change it to a tell event.game call if you write it in the game script)

> on enter do

To explain the idea, PULP only stops the execution at the end of events, so you need 2 events calling each other in a loop to get the "waiting for keypress" effect!

[CoronaVitae](https://devforum.play.date/u/CoronaVitae)  July 17, 2022, 2:47pm 16 

Yeah, that's the issue with wait. If you use "say...then" it will wait for confirmation...but only for whatever is between "then" and "end."

You can work around this by using event calls as discussed above, but things start getting complicated when you start mixing in functions.

Normally you would add "then call "dialogue2"" to the say event in the dislogue tile, but you don't want dialoguetile to call the event, you want the original tile to call the event. There is a super hacky way to do that: if the dialogue tile is not placed anywhere, it takes the last event.x, event.y that was available, in this case the original tile (this is undocumented, maybe a glitch, but I'm pretty sure this works based on testing).

So you could make the dialoguetile script:

Wait a then  
say "txt" then  
wait b then  
tell event.x, event.y to call "{nexttext}"  
end  
end  
end

and change your original script to

a=  
b=  
nexttext=\[next event name\]  
tell dialogue to  
call "display"  
end//(must be end of event)

# [ Playdate Simulator](/manual/simulator/) 

The Playdate Simulator is an application that mimics the Playdate device, and makes Playdate development quick and easy on macOS, Windows, and Linux. The Simulator not only runs Playdate applications, but can also emulate the functionality of Playdate’s controls, including its crank and accelerometer.

### Table of Contents

![Playdate Simulator](/manual/simulator/simulator2@2x.jpg "Playdate Simulator") 

Playdate Simulator

## Controls

Games running in the simulator can be controlled by the on-screen GUI, or keyboard shortcuts. The simulator can also be controlled by a select number of compatible game controllers, or the Playdate console itself, if connected.

You can switch between several control schemes in the Controls menu. These will change which keyboard buttons control the d-pad and the A and B buttons.

You can also configure compatible game controllers in Preferences.

![Controller preferences in the Playdate Simulator](/manual/simulator/controller@2x.png "Controller preferences in the Playdate Simulator") 

Controller preferences in the Playdate Simulator

### Crank and Accelerometer

The Simulator includes a GUI for approximating control of the device’s accelerometer and crank inputs.

![Crank and Accelerometer controls in the Playdate Simulator](/manual/simulator/crank-and-accel@2x.png "Crank and Accelerometer controls in the Playdate Simulator") 

Crank and Accelerometer controls in the Playdate Simulator

Drag the controls to control these inputs. You can also control the crank using the [keyboard](#keyboard-shortcuts), or by scrolling the scroll wheel on your mouse or other pointing device. Double-clicking the crank circle will let you turn it just by moving your mouse.

Games can tell whether the crank is [docked or not](https://sdk.play.date/inside-playdate/#f-isCrankDocked); there is also a checkbox control to simulate this. You can enter the crank angle manually, or use the slider to set a constant rotation forward or backward.

## Device menu

When you connect a Playdate to your computer, you can use a number of device features from the Simulator. Here’s you how access the device menu:

* Connect your Playdate to your computer via USB cable.
* Unlock your Playdate by pressing the Lock button on Playdate’s top edge.

* **On macOS**, press the Playdate button that appears in the lower right corner of the Simulator window. {.platform .platform-mac}

* **On Windows and Linux**, open the Device menu in the menu bar.

![Device menu in the Playdate Simulator](/manual/simulator/device-menu@2x.png "Device menu in the Playdate Simulator") 

Device menu in the Playdate Simulator

### Using your Playdate to control the Simulator

If you enjoy the rapid development the Playdate Simulator offers, while also wanting the tactile feel of Playdate controls, you can put your Playdate device into controller mode to control the Simulator with your Playdate hardware.

Choose the Device > Use Device as Controller option in the above menu. Your Playdate’s inputs will now control the Simulator.

**On macOS**, there is also a reverse option: Device > Control Device with Simulator. This may be useful when testing a feature that’s easier to control or reproduce with computer input.

### Uploading games from the Simulator

Using this will upload the currently loaded .pdx to the device. It will overwrite the .pdx of the same name if it exists on the device.

**On macOS**, this will essentially merge the two bundles, so any files that were present in the old .pdx on the device will remain, and existing files will be overwritten with new ones.

This upload process may take some time with larger games.

## Performance

Game performance is considerably faster in the Simulator than on the Playdate hardware. Please take that into consideration when developing your game, and make sure to periodically test on Playdate hardware.

You can learn a lot about your code’s performance by using the [debugging features](#debugging) of the Simulator.

### Throttling Lua performance

If you're on macOS and you enable the Playdate > Throttle Lua Performance option, the Simulator will run Lua code slower than usual. This won't accurately mimic device speed, but it may slow down execution enough for you to detect problem areas in your game.

## Appearance

### Highlighting screen updates

A major way to improve the performance of your game is to not redraw the screen more than is needed. You can check how much of the screen is being redrawn in your game if you enable the Playdate > Highlight Screen Updates option:

![Highlight Screen Updates in the Playdate Simulator](/manual/simulator/screen-updates.png "Highlight Screen Updates in the Playdate Simulator") 

Highlight Screen Updates in the Playdate Simulator

This is particularly useful—and your code will likely run more efficiently—if you take advantage of our [sprite system](https://sdk.play.date/inside-playdate/#C-graphics.sprite), which tracks which areas should be redrawn.

### Showing sprite collision rects

Enabling the Playdate > Show Sprite Collision Rects option is a good way to debug your [collisions](https://sdk.play.date/inside-playdate/#M-sprite-collisions).

### Debug Drawing

If your code implements [playdate.debugDraw](https://sdk.play.date/inside-playdate/#c-debugDraw), you can turn its display on and off in the Playdate menu on Windows and Linux.

### Simulating device appearance

Enabling Playdate > Simulate Device Appearance will do the following:

* The Simulator window will become yellow, to match the color of the Playdate hardware.
* The display will use two gray colors instead of pure black and pure white, to match the Memory LCD display on the hardware
* Screenshots and GIFs you save will use these gray colors as well.

![Simulated device appearance in the Playdate Simulator](/manual/simulator/simulate@2x.png "Simulated device appearance in the Playdate Simulator") 

Simulated device appearance in the Playdate Simulator

## Saving screenshots and GIFs

With your game running or paused, you can take a screenshot of it by using the “photo camera” button in the toolbar. You’ll be presented with a dialog to save this as a PNG image. Holding down the Option/Alt button while clicking the Screenshot button will copy the image to your clipboard instead of saving a file.

While your game is running, click the “video camera” button in the toolbar to begin recording a GIF animation of the display.

![Screenshot and GIF buttons in the Playdate Simulator](/manual/simulator/screenshot-buttons.png "Screenshot and GIF buttons in the Playdate Simulator") 

Screenshot and GIF buttons in the Playdate Simulator

**Note:** Screenshots and GIFs will use simulated device appearance (gray colors) if this function is [enabled](#simulating-device-appearance).

**Note:** GIFs won’t record your game’s sound. If you’d like to capture a video with sound, you can use our [Mirror](https://play.date/mirror) app, or a screen-recording app.

**Note:** Overlays such as [screen-update highlights](#highlighting-screen-updates), [collision rects](#showing-sprite-collision-rects), and [debug draws](https://sdk.play.date/inside-playdate/#c-debugDraw) won’t be saved with your screenshots and GIFs. Game recordings will be saved as they would appear to players.

## Debugging

The Playdate Simulator includes a number of tools for measuring, inspecting, and debugging your running code. These are separate windows, available from the Window menu and the toolbar.

![Debugging tools in the Playdate Simulator](/manual/simulator/tools.png "Debugging tools in the Playdate Simulator") 

Debugging tools in the Playdate Simulator

* **Lua Memory**. Shows all the Lua objects taking up your game’s memory. **Note**: this tool is available only while your game is paused.
* **Malloc Log**. Shows the memory usage by your C code.
* **Device Info**. When a Playdate is [connected to your computer](#device-menu), this tools shows a variety of graphs outlining its performance and memory usage.
* **Console**. Displays logs printed from your code, and lets you enter commands to evaluate in real time.
* **Sampler**. Lets you sample a running game to see where your code is spending most of its time.

* **Event Recorder**. On macOS, this lets you record user input and play it back. Useful for recreating a particular set of steps your game goes through.

## Debug adapter protocol

The Playdate Simulator supports the [debug adapter protocol](https://microsoft.github.io/debug-adapter-protocol/), which makes it possible to debug execution line by line from your code editor, such as [Nova](https://nova.app).

## Keyboard shortcuts

| Action               | Shortcut    |
| -------------------- | ----------- |
| Restart              | Cmd/Ctrl-R  |
| Pause                | Space       |
| Lock                 | Cmd/Ctrl-L  |
| Menu                 | Escape      |
| Crank Forward        | \[          |
| Crank Backward       | \]          |
| Volume Down          | \-          |
| Volume Up            | \=          |
| Toggle Full Screen   | Fn-F        |
| Rotate Display Left  | Cmd/Ctrl ◀︎ |
| Rotate Display Right | Cmd/Ctrl ▶︎ |
| 2x Display           | Cmd/Ctrl-2  |

[If you didn't find an answer above, contact us](/contact/)

# Playdate Debug

[![tests](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/actions/workflows/tests.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/actions/workflows/tests.yaml)

Unofficial Playdate debug extension for Visual Studio Code on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu

## Features

- Debug Lua code running in the Playdate Simulator
- Compile games to `.pdx` using `pdc`
- Problem matchers for `pdc`
- Open the Playdate Simulator
- Run and debug current Lua file in the Playdate Simulator from the editor toolbar

## Requirements

- The [Playdate SDK](https://play.date/dev/) must be installed separately

## Quick setup

### Tasks and debug launcher

Copy the following `.vscode/tasks.json` and `.vscode/launch.json` configuration:

```json
// .vscode/tasks.json
{
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "tasks": [
    {
      "type": "pdc",
      "problemMatcher": ["$pdc-lua", "$pdc-external"],
      "label": "Playdate: Build"
    },
    {
      "type": "playdate-simulator",
      "problemMatcher": ["$pdc-external"],
      "label": "Playdate: Run"
    },
    {
      "label": "Playdate: Build and Run",
      "dependsOn": ["Playdate: Build", "Playdate: Run"],
      "dependsOrder": "sequence",
      "problemMatcher": [],
      "group": {
        "kind": "build",
        "isDefault": true
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

```json
// .vscode/launch.json
{
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "configurations": [
    {
      "type": "playdate",
      "request": "launch",
      "name": "Playdate: Debug",
      "preLaunchTask": "${defaultBuildTask}"
    }
  ]
}
```

The debugger can be launched from the "Run and Debug view" by selecting the "Playdate: Debug" launch configuration and then clicking the "Start Debugging" button.

![Run and Debug view](/images/run-and-debug-view.png)

![Start Debugging](/images/start-debugging.png)

A [cookiecutter project template](https://github.com/midouest/cookiecutter-playdate) is available for quickly generating new projects with the above configuration from the command line.

See the [basic configuration example](/fixtures/workspace/basic-configuration) for more information.

### Run and debug current Lua file

**NOTE:** The "Run/Debug file in Playdate Simulator" command is intended to be a shortcut for prototyping and learning. It is recommended to use the [task and launch configuration above](#tasks-and-debug-launcher).

The extension can build, run and debug the current Lua file in the editor with zero configuration as long the [automatic configuration conditions](#automatic) are met.

When you open a Lua file in the editor after installing the extension, you will now see a
launch icon and dropdown menu in the editor toolbar. Clicking the launch icon or selecting an item from the dropdown menu will build and run the current Lua file in the Playdate Simulator. The "Debug file in Playdate Simulator" option will enable breakpoints to be hit.

![Tooltip](/images/tooltip.png)

![Dropdown Menu](/images/dropdown-menu.png)

## Configuration

### Automatic

The tasks and debugger will attempt to automatically resolve the correct configuration using the environment. One of the following conditions must be met for this to work:

- The `PLAYDATE_SDK_PATH` environment variable is set to the Playdate SDK path
- `~/.Playdate/config` exists and the `SDKRoot` property is set to the Playdate SDK path (macOS only)

### Workspace settings override

The default behavior can be overridden by setting the SDK path, game source path, compiled game path or game name in your workspace's `settings.json` file. The extension will fall back to the default behavior for any configuration fields that are not set.

```json
// .vscode/settings.json
{
  "playdate-debug.sdkPath": "/path/to/PlaydateSDK",
  "playdate-debug.sourcePath": "/path/to/MyGame/source",
  "playdate-debug.outputPath": "/path/to/MyGame",
  "playdate-debug.productName": "My Game"
}
```

See the [override configuration example](/fixtures/workspace/override-configuration) for more information about these properties.

### PDC task

See the [pdc configuration example](/fixtures/workspace/pdc-configuration/) for additional `pdc` task properties.

### Playdate Simulator task

See the [playdate simulator configuration example](/fixtures/workspace/playdate-simulator-configuration/) for additional `playdate-simulator` task properties.

### Debugger

See the [debugger configuration example](/fixtures/workspace/debugger-configuration/) for additional `playdate` debugger properties.

# Playdate Debug

[![tests](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/actions/workflows/tests.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/actions/workflows/tests.yaml)

Unofficial Playdate debug extension for Visual Studio Code on macOS, Windows and Ubuntu

## Features

* Debug Lua code running in the Playdate Simulator
* Compile games to `.pdx` using `pdc`
* Problem matchers for `pdc`
* Open the Playdate Simulator
* Run and debug current Lua file in the Playdate Simulator from the editor toolbar

## Requirements

* The [Playdate SDK](https://play.date/dev/) must be installed separately

## Quick setup

### Tasks and debug launcher

Copy the following `.vscode/tasks.json` and `.vscode/launch.json` configuration:

// .vscode/tasks.json
{
  "version": "2.0.0",
  "tasks": [
    {
      "type": "pdc",
      "problemMatcher": ["$pdc-lua", "$pdc-external"],
      "label": "Playdate: Build"
    },
    {
      "type": "playdate-simulator",
      "problemMatcher": ["$pdc-external"],
      "label": "Playdate: Run"
    },
    {
      "label": "Playdate: Build and Run",
      "dependsOn": ["Playdate: Build", "Playdate: Run"],
      "dependsOrder": "sequence",
      "problemMatcher": [],
      "group": {
        "kind": "build",
        "isDefault": true
      }
    }
  ]
}

// .vscode/launch.json
{
  "version": "0.2.0",
  "configurations": [
    {
      "type": "playdate",
      "request": "launch",
      "name": "Playdate: Debug",
      "preLaunchTask": "${defaultBuildTask}"
    }
  ]
}

The debugger can be launched from the "Run and Debug view" by selecting the "Playdate: Debug" launch configuration and then clicking the "Start Debugging" button.

[![Run and Debug view](/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/raw/main/images/run-and-debug-view.png)](/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/images/run-and-debug-view.png)

[![Start Debugging](/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/raw/main/images/start-debugging.png)](/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/images/start-debugging.png)

A [cookiecutter project template](https://github.com/midouest/cookiecutter-playdate) is available for quickly generating new projects with the above configuration from the command line.

See the [basic configuration example](/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/fixtures/workspace/basic-configuration) for more information.

### Run and debug current Lua file

**NOTE:** The "Run/Debug file in Playdate Simulator" command is intended to be a shortcut for prototyping and learning. It is recommended to use the [task and launch configuration above](#tasks-and-debug-launcher).

The extension can build, run and debug the current Lua file in the editor with zero configuration as long the [automatic configuration conditions](#automatic) are met.

When you open a Lua file in the editor after installing the extension, you will now see a launch icon and dropdown menu in the editor toolbar. Clicking the launch icon or selecting an item from the dropdown menu will build and run the current Lua file in the Playdate Simulator. The "Debug file in Playdate Simulator" option will enable breakpoints to be hit.

[![Tooltip](/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/raw/main/images/tooltip.png)](/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/images/tooltip.png)

[![Dropdown Menu](/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/raw/main/images/dropdown-menu.png)](/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/images/dropdown-menu.png)

## Configuration

### Automatic

The tasks and debugger will attempt to automatically resolve the correct configuration using the environment. One of the following conditions must be met for this to work:

* The `PLAYDATE_SDK_PATH` environment variable is set to the Playdate SDK path
* `~/.Playdate/config` exists and the `SDKRoot` property is set to the Playdate SDK path (macOS only)

### Workspace settings override

The default behavior can be overridden by setting the SDK path, game source path, compiled game path or game name in your workspace's `settings.json` file. The extension will fall back to the default behavior for any configuration fields that are not set.

// .vscode/settings.json
{
  "playdate-debug.sdkPath": "/path/to/PlaydateSDK",
  "playdate-debug.sourcePath": "/path/to/MyGame/source",
  "playdate-debug.outputPath": "/path/to/MyGame",
  "playdate-debug.productName": "My Game"
}

See the [override configuration example](/midouest/vscode-playdate-debug/blob/main/fixtures/workspace/override-configuration) for more information about these properties.
